_README: WEEKLY JUDICIAL TIP-OFF FEEDS. Read app/sources/judicial_feeds.py before editing.
WHAT THIS IS. A list of RSS feeds that tell a reviewer THAT a court has
published something that may touch an instrument Legafy tracks. That is all.
A lead from here is never a citation, never enters the grounding matrix, and
never moves a traffic-light lane. It ends up in a human's reading queue.
WHY indiankanoon.org AND NOT THE COURTS' OWN SITES. The courts publish
judgments, but most do not publish a machine-readable feed of them. Indian
Kanoon does, per court. It is an AGGREGATOR (authority weight 0.25, below the
0.80 citable floor), so it is fit to say 'go look', and unfit to be quoted.
The reviewer's job is to open the judgment on the COURT's own site before
anything reaches a user.
EVERY SLUG BELOW WAS READ OFF https://indiankanoon.org/feeds/ ON 2026-09-14,
not guessed. A guessed slug returns HTTP 404, and an empty feed and a wrong
URL look identical in a weekly report — which is how a court silently stops
being watched. `make judicial-check` re-verifies every slug; run it before
trusting a quiet week.
PERMISSION. robots.txt at indiankanoon.org does not disallow /feeds/, so
reading these is permitted. It DOES disallow many /doc/ paths — so this
module reads the feed and never follows the link to fetch a judgment body.
Metadata and a pointer only. Before relying on this commercially, get written
confirmation from Indian Kanoon; absence of a prohibition is not a licence.

feeds.note: Binding on every High Court. A change here outranks any state reading.
